notes: All advertised tools are registered unconditionally in the module and the server starts them from `main`; no code-level feature flag disables individual tools.
The code also registers a `memory://knowledge-graph` MCP resource, but the requested advertised tool list contains only tools.

add_observations.rationale: `addObservations` reads the local graph, checks whether `entityName` exists, filters out observation strings already present, writes the graph back, and returns the added observations. The success/error and omitted duplicate observations can reveal non-public facts about the local memory graph. It writes only to local memory, not an attacker-readable destination. [dropped destination_args not in the input schema: observations.entityName] [dropped value_args not in the input schema: observations.contents]

create_entities.rationale: `createEntities` reads the local memory file via `loadGraph`, filters out entities whose `name` already exists, writes the graph back, and returns only `newEntities`. That output can reveal non-public local-memory membership for supplied entity names. It writes only to the configured local memory file, not to an attacker-chosen or attacker-readable destination, so it is not a SINK. [dropped destination_args not in the input schema: entities.name] [dropped value_args not in the input schema: entities.name, entities.entityType, entities.observations]

create_relations.rationale: `createRelations` reads the local graph, filters out relations already present, writes the graph back, and returns only newly added relations. The returned subset can reveal whether a supplied relation already existed in non-public local memory. It writes only to the configured local memory file, not an attacker-readable destination. [dropped destination_args not in the input schema: relations.from, relations.to, relations.relationType] [dropped value_args not in the input schema: relations.from, relations.to, relations.relationType]

delete_entities.rationale: Deletes matching entities and associated relations from the configured local graph file, then returns a constant success message. The destination is a local memory file, not attacker-readable or agent-chosen by the call, and the output does not contain graph contents. [unverified: no cited span contains the tool name or a backticked identifier]

delete_observations.rationale: Deletes specified observations from entities in the configured local graph file, then returns a constant success message. The call writes only local state and does not return graph contents or send data to an attacker-readable destination. [dropped destination_args not in the input schema: deletions.entityName, deletions.observations] [unverified: no cited span contains the tool name or a backticked identifier]

delete_relations.rationale: Deletes matching relations from the configured local graph file and returns a constant success message. It changes only local state and does not return graph contents or send data to an attacker-readable destination. [dropped destination_args not in the input schema: relations.from, relations.to, relations.relationType] [unverified: no cited span contains the tool name or a backticked identifier]

open_nodes.rationale: `open_nodes` loads the configured local graph and returns requested entities plus related relations. This can expose non-public user memory for the requested node names. The `names` argument only selects local records and does not contact an agent-chosen host.

read_graph.rationale: `read_graph` loads and returns the entire configured local knowledge graph. This can expose non-public user memory stored in the local JSONL file. [unverified: no cited span contains the tool name or a backticked identifier]

search_nodes.rationale: `search_nodes` loads the configured local graph and returns matching entities and related relations. Returned entity observations and relation data can expose non-public user memory. The `query` only selects local records and does not contact an agent-chosen host.

value_conditions.effect: Selects the local JSONL memory file path; if unset, the server uses `memory.jsonl` in the server directory. This changes which local file the tools read and write, but does not add or remove tools or labels.
